name: Realistic All-In Cost to Convert a Garage to a Legal ADU in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What are realistic all-in costs to convert a detached garage into a code-compliant ADU in Los Angeles County, including permits, utility upgrades, and required seismic work?
mainEntity.text: What are realistic all-in costs to convert a detached garage into a code-compliant ADU in Los Angeles County, including permits, utility upgrades, and required seismic work?

acceptedAnswer.text: A garage-to-ADU conversion in Los Angeles County often costs substantially more than basic “per square foot” estimates suggest because many hidden items are not included in headline numbers. Realistic budgets usually combine: - **Construction and finishes**: framing, insulation, doors, windows, roofing, drywall, flooring, cabinets, and fixtures. Upgrading to residential-quality windows, doors, and insulation to meet energy codes can be a major jump from a basic garage structure. - **Design and engineering**: architectural plans, structural engineering (especially for roof modifications, new openings, or seismic reinforcement), and title-24 energy calculations. - **Permits and fees**: building permits, plan check fees, and city or county impact or school fees when applicable. Some cities reduce or waive certain fees for smaller ADUs, but not all. - **Utilities and site work**: new plumbing drains to the main sewer line, water supply, electrical subpanel or service upgrade, gas line (if used), trenching, and possible separate meters. Many older garages need panel upgrades to support full-time residential use. - **Seismic and foundation work**: anchoring the existing structure, adding hold-downs, reinforcing cripple walls, and repairing or thickening slabs where required. Ask contractors for **itemized bids** that clearly separate these categories, and confirm whether utility trenching, fees, and engineering are included or listed as allowances.
acceptedAnswer.description: Total costs to convert a detached garage into a legal ADU in Los Angeles County typically include construction, design, permits, impact and utility fees, and possible seismic or foundation upgrades. Budgets should account for structural reinforcement, new plumbing and electrical runs, insulation, heating/cooling, and separate utility meters if required by local codes or your design.
